old:
The control changes addressed the problems found during bring-up. PA1
voltage regulation replaced the incorrect power feedback, with PA2 retained
for load classification. Complete-cycle scheduling addressed irregular
pulses, and no-load guarding limited charging after load removal. Measurement review separated waveform ripple from the
spread of acquisition averages. The original readings give a maximum
calculated output of \SI{79.89}{\watt}; further loading toward the
\SI{100}{\watt} objective requires temperature histories alongside the
electrical readings.
new:
PA1 voltage regulation replaced the incorrect power feedback, while PA2
was retained for load classification. Complete-cycle scheduling addressed
irregular pulses, and no-load guarding limited charging after load removal.
The highest calculated output was \SI{79.89}{\watt}; further loading toward
the \SI{100}{\watt} objective requires temperature histories alongside the
electrical readings.
reason: Connects the implemented corrections and removes repetition of the ripple-statistics distinction already explained in steady-state results.
facts_preserved: PA1, PA2, complete-cycle scheduling, no-load guarding, 79.89 W and 100 W target retained.

old:
Chapter~\ref{ch:results} reports selected fixed outputs and matched
measurements near \SI{80}{\watt}. Average voltage regulation was maintained,
but ripple, load-dependent input-current quality, and surface heating
remained.

The most complete high-power measurements cover \SI{20}{\volt} at
\SIrange{3.7}{4.0}{\ampere}, giving \SIrange{73.97}{79.89}{\watt}
and an initial efficiency estimate of \SIrange{76.5}{77.1}{\percent}.
Average USB-C output voltage was maintained across these points. The input--output
power difference and surface heating point to losses within the power path.
Simultaneous stage-power and temperature measurements would locate those losses.
new:
At \SI{20}{\volt} and \SIrange{3.7}{4.0}{\ampere}, the most complete
high-power measurements gave \SIrange{73.97}{79.89}{\watt} and an initial
efficiency estimate of \SIrange{76.5}{77.1}{\percent}. Average USB-C output
voltage remained regulated, while ripple, load-dependent input-current quality,
and surface heating remained. The input--output power difference and heating
point to losses in the power path; simultaneous stage-power and temperature
measurements would help locate them.
reason: Combines overlapping descriptions of the same results and links the remaining loss measurement to the observation.
facts_preserved: 20 V, 3.7–4.0 A, 73.97–79.89 W, initial efficiency and unresolved losses retained.

old:
Mean output voltage was maintained at the tested loads, while ripple and
input-current quality remained load-dependent. Burst spacing and fixed
losses influence performance at low demand; current stress and heating become more
significant at high demand. The best PF and THD were measured at the highest loads on the
\SI{20}{\volt} output. Control and hardware changes must therefore be assessed
across the charge pump, burst schedule, secondary bulk supply, USB-C PD
output stage, and thermal path.
new:
Mean output voltage was maintained at the tested loads, while ripple and
input-current quality varied with load. Burst spacing and fixed losses affect
low-demand performance, while current stress and heating become more significant
at high demand. The best PF and THD were measured at the highest loads on the
\SI{20}{\volt} output. Changes to the charge pump or burst schedule should
therefore be assessed together with their effects on both output stages and heating.
reason: Connects the operating trade-off to the reason for assessing hardware and control changes together.
facts_preserved: Load-dependent ripple and current quality, best PF and THD at highest 20 V loads, and thermal implications retained.

old:

\SI{65}{\watt} continuous as the minimum \cite{projectOctoberPlan}.
Defined-duration tests with temperature histories are still needed at these

approximately \SI{85}{\watt} V2 point should be repeated with the board,
firmware, settings, power readings, and temperatures recorded together.
This earlier V2 point is separate from the calculated \SI{79.89}{\watt}
V1.0 result above.
new:
The target remains \SI{100}{\watt} continuous, with a minimum of
\SI{65}{\watt} \cite{projectOctoberPlan}. Defined-duration tests with
temperature histories are needed to assess sustained operation at these
levels.
reason: Focuses the conclusion on the target and the measurements needed for sustained operation; detailed V1 and V2 comparisons appear in the results and discussion.
facts_preserved: 100 W target and 65 W minimum retained; earlier 75 W milestone and approximately 85 W V2 result remain in the results and discussion.
